title: Fly Me High — Internal Operations Platform
summary: The first internal software for a small travel company that ran on spreadsheets: a backend system for customer records, prospects, and operational handoffs, built as their first full-time technical hire.
problem: Fly Me High is a travel company, not a software company. Sales and operations lived in spreadsheets and manual steps — customer records, prospects, handoffs between people — which was slow, easy to get wrong, and impossible to see across. There was no internal product because there had never been anyone to build one.
approach: As the first full-time technical hire, I started by learning how the business actually worked, then turned those workflow pains into requirements. I designed the backend architecture and built the internal system in Java / Spring Boot on PostgreSQL, exposing REST APIs I tested and debugged in Postman. I also coordinated roughly four frontend interns — defining tasks, setting roadmap priorities, and supporting releases and the internal users who depended on it day to day.
outcome: Replaced manual spreadsheet workflows with an internal product: roughly 30 minutes less processing time per customer record, adoption growing from about 3 users to 6–7 across the team, and ~25% faster backend responses after targeted API debugging.
role: Software Developer — first full-time technical hire
